item.text:
“the stakes for our company has never been higher” >>> “the stakes for our company have never been higher”

“the federal goverment” >>> “the federal government”

“more then ever” >>> “more than ever”

“has three cosponsors on the committee, Senators Okafor and Lindqvist” >>> [CHECK: Three cosponsors are claimed, but only two are named.]

“it's definitions are broad” >>> “its definitions are broad”

“its central principal” >>> “its central principle”

“In brief, the bill:” >>> “In brief:”

“the bill's enforcment regime” >>> “the bill's enforcement regime”

“would directly effect every company” >>> “would directly affect every company”

“Senator Whitfield (R-OK)” >>> [CHECK: Whitfield is identified as R-OH earlier.]

“the registry in Section 5” >>> “the registry in Section 4”

“keeps the $10 million daily civil penalty in Section 5” >>> [CHECK: The earlier summary specifies a maximum daily civil penalty of $1 million, not $10 million.]

“who's support may depend on it” >>> “whose support may depend on it”

“the amendment's changes is modest” >>> “the amendment's changes are modest”

“of the committees 28 members” >>> “of the committee's 28 members”

“13 are yes or leaning yes, 10 are no or leaning no, and 6 are undecided” >>> [CHECK: These counts total 29, but the committee is said to have 28 members.]

“The undecided senators are Chen, Ellis, Alvarez, Pike, and Barlow.” >>> [CHECK: Only five senators are listed, versus six undecided in the preceding sentence. Kowalski and Ames are also subsequently described as not having committed to a final position; clarify their classifications.]

“Thursday, October 14” >>> “Thursday, October 15”

“in a seperate interview” >>> “in a separate interview”

“The list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, are attached.” >>> “The list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, is attached.”

“Commerce Commitee markup” >>> “Commerce Committee markup”

“the week November 16” >>> “the week of November 16”

“the committee's hearing on the risks of advanced AI occured on September 30” >>> [CHECK: “Occured” should be “occurred”; the votes section dates a hearing to September 23. Confirm whether these are different hearings or correct the inconsistent date.]

“would have to conclude within two years” >>> [CHECK: The Section 6 summary specifies 18 months, not two years.]

“a close compliment to S. 2817” >>> “a close complement to S. 2817”

“with the the offices” >>> “with the offices”

“call there senators” >>> “call their senators”

“you should recieve updated talking points” >>> “you should receive updated talking points”

“Each of our five regional policy leads” >>> [CHECK: The preceding paragraph says there are six regional policy leads.]
